source: Phaladeepika Ch. 8 (the grahas in the twelve bhavas from the Lagna), in Sudarshana's words
note: These are the results the classic gives for a graha in each bhava by itself. A graha strong by sign, in its own or exaltation sign, or aspected by benefics gives its good results more fully and its bad ones less, and a weak or afflicted one the reverse; Rahu gives results like Saturn's and Ketu like Mars's (Phaladeepika 8.34-35).

Su.text: The Sun in the Lagna makes the native proud, brave and impatient, with little hair, a bilious, heated body and eyes that may be weak; they want to lead and dislike being ruled.
In the 2nd the Sun can trouble the face, eyes or teeth and stir quarrels in the family; wealth comes through the state or those in authority, but goes on standing and display.
In the 3rd, an upachaya, the Sun gives valour, intelligence, wealth and success by one's own effort; younger brothers and sisters may suffer or be few.
In the 4th the Sun disturbs home and heart: little peace, strain with relatives and over land and houses; the native may serve the state and lose ancestral property.
In the 5th the Sun gives a sharp intelligence but few children and worry through them; the mind is proud, and fortune comes through authority.
In the 6th, an upachaya, the Sun is strong: victory over enemies, fame and authority, good digestion and success in service and litigation.
In the 7th the Sun brings wandering, strain in or loss of marriage, and humiliation through others.
In the 8th the Sun takes away wealth and friends, shortens life and harms the eyesight.
In the 9th the Sun may take the father early, but gives children and kin, and reverence for the gods and for Brahmins.
In the 10th, where it has dig bala, the Sun gives sons, vehicles, praise, intelligence, wealth, strength and fame: the native rises to rule.
In the 11th the Sun gives great wealth and a long life, royal standing and freedom from sorrow.
In the 12th the Sun sets the native against the father, weakens the eyes and leaves them short of wealth and children.

Mo.text: Waxing in the Lagna the Moon gives a strong body, long life, fearlessness, power and wealth; waning, the reverse.
In the 2nd the Moon makes the native rich, learned and soft-spoken and fond of pleasure, though with some defect of a limb.
In the 3rd the Moon gives brothers, strength and power, a passionate nature and a miserly hand.
In the 4th, where it has dig bala, the Moon gives happiness and pleasures, generosity, friends, vehicles and renown.
In the 5th the Moon gives good children and a sharp intelligence, a gentle bearing and a minister's place.
In the 6th the Moon gives a short life, little learning, troubles of the stomach and humiliation.
In the 7th the Moon makes the native pleasing to see and loved by a beautiful partner.
In the 8th the Moon brings disease and a short life.
In the 9th the Moon gives prosperity, virtue, children and victory; undertakings succeed from the start.
In the 10th the Moon makes the native do good deeds and help the virtuous.
In the 11th the Moon gives a lofty mind, a long life, wealth, children and servants.
In the 12th the Moon makes the native disliked, miserable, insulted and idle.

Ma.text: In the Lagna Mars brings injury to a limb and a short life, and a cruel, adventurous nature.
In the 2nd Mars spoils the face and speech and leaves the native without learning or wealth, dependent on bad people.
In the 3rd Mars gives good qualities, wealth, bravery, invincibility and happiness, but no brothers.
In the 4th Mars takes away friends, mother, lands, happiness and vehicles.
In the 5th Mars brings unhappiness, few or no children, reverses, a backbiting tongue and a weak mind.
In the 6th Mars gives passion, wealth and fame: a ruler victorious in battle.
In the 7th Mars leads to improper acts, disease and wandering, and to loss of the spouse.
In the 8th Mars gives a deformed body, poverty, a short life and the curses of others.
In the 9th Mars makes the native hated though befriended by the ruler, fatherless, and capable of violence.
In the 10th Mars makes a cruel but liberal ruler, praised by the great.
In the 11th Mars gives riches and happiness, bravery, freedom from sorrow and good character.
In the 12th Mars harms the eyes and makes the native cruel, without a spouse, a slanderer and mean.

Me.text: In the Lagna Mercury gives a long life, sweet and clever speech, a sharp wit and learning in all the Shastras.
In the 2nd Mercury earns wealth by talent: the native is a poet, sincere and attractive, and fond of rich food.
In the 3rd Mercury makes the native brave, with good brothers and a middling life, but often tired and dejected.
In the 4th Mercury gives learning and wit, happiness, friends, lands, grain, wealth and enjoyment.
In the 5th Mercury gives learning, happiness, courage, many children and skill in mantras.
In the 6th Mercury makes the native quarrelsome, harsh of speech and idle, yet able to break the enemies' power.
In the 7th Mercury gives learning, fine dress and greatness, and a rich spouse.
In the 8th Mercury gives wide renown and a long life; the native supports the family and may command an army.
In the 9th Mercury makes the native learned, wealthy, well-behaved, religious and eloquent.
In the 10th Mercury brings success in undertakings, learning, strength, intelligence, happiness and truthfulness.
In the 11th Mercury gives a long life, truthfulness, great wealth, happiness and servants.
In the 12th Mercury makes the native miserable, unlearned, humiliated, cruel and inactive.

Ju.text: In the Lagna Jupiter gives a handsome body, good fortune, a long life, fearlessness and children.
In the 2nd Jupiter gives eloquence, a fine taste in food, a lovely face, wealth and learning.
In the 3rd Jupiter brings disrespect and miserliness and a sinful, ill-disposed turn, though a brother may be renowned.
In the 4th Jupiter gives a happy life with mother, friends, servants, children, spouse and plenty of grain.
In the 5th Jupiter, the karaka of children, brings trouble through children (the karaka harming its own bhava), yet gives intelligence and a place as adviser to the ruler.
In the 6th Jupiter makes the native inactive and disrespected, but victorious over enemies and skilled in mantras and exorcism.
In the 7th Jupiter gives a good spouse and children, an amiable nature and more generosity than the father had.
In the 8th Jupiter gives a long life but poverty, menial work and a sinful turn.
In the 9th Jupiter makes the native a famous minister, wealthy, with children and devoted to virtuous acts.
In the 10th Jupiter gives right conduct, renowned virtues, great wealth and the friendship of the ruler.
In the 11th Jupiter gives wealth, fearlessness, a long life and vehicles, but few children.
In the 12th Jupiter makes the native disliked, foul-mouthed, childless, sinful, idle and menial.

Ve.text: In the Lagna Venus gives health, a beautiful body, happiness and a long life.
In the 2nd Venus makes the native a poet with riches of many kinds.
In the 3rd Venus leaves the native without a spouse, unhappy, poor, miserly and unpopular.
In the 4th Venus gives fine vehicles, a good house, jewels, clothes and perfumes.
In the 5th Venus gives immense wealth, wisdom and children, and the power to protect others.
In the 6th Venus leaves the native without enemies but without riches, led astray by the young and grieving.
In the 7th Venus, the karaka of the spouse, gives a good partner and wealth, but affairs with others and the loss of a spouse (the karaka harming its own bhava).
In the 8th Venus gives a long life, wealth and lordship.
In the 9th Venus gives a spouse, friends and children, and prosperity through royal favour.
In the 10th Venus gives wide renown, friends and a happy, lordly position.
In the 11th Venus gives riches, the company of women and many comforts.
In the 12th Venus gives the pleasures of the bed, wealth and splendour.

Sa.text: In the Lagna Saturn in its own or exaltation sign makes the native equal to a king or the head of a city; elsewhere it brings sorrow, poverty, slovenliness and indolence.
In the 2nd Saturn spoils the face and leaves the native without wealth and given to evil ways; later in life they live abroad with vehicles and wealth.
In the 3rd Saturn makes the native intelligent, generous and happy with the spouse, but inactive and sorrowful.
In the 4th Saturn brings unhappiness, no home or vehicles, loss of the mother and illness in childhood.
In the 5th Saturn makes the native wandering and unsettled of mind, childless, short of happiness and treacherous.
In the 6th Saturn makes the native voracious, wealthy, stubborn and self-respecting, though troubled by enemies.
In the 7th Saturn brings a difficult spouse, poverty, wandering and distress.
In the 8th Saturn, the karaka of longevity, brings uncleanliness, poverty, piles, cruelty and hunger, and the contempt of friends.
In the 9th Saturn leaves the native without fortune, wealth, children, father or religious merit.
In the 10th Saturn makes the native a ruler or minister, brave, rich and renowned, working with the land.
In the 11th Saturn gives a long life, lasting wealth, a good income, bravery and freedom from disease.
In the 12th Saturn makes the native impudent, poor and childless, with a defect of a limb, dull, and driven out by enemies.

Ra.text: In the Lagna Rahu gives wealth and strength but a short life and diseases of the head and face.
In the 2nd Rahu makes speech insincere and brings disease to the mouth or face; the native is tender-hearted but wrathful, with wealth from the ruler.
In the 3rd Rahu makes the native proud, strong-willed, long-lived and wealthy, but hostile to brothers.
In the 4th Rahu makes the native foolish and a cause of sorrow, with friends and a short life, happy only at times.
In the 5th Rahu brings few or no children, a hard heart, pains in the stomach and a nasal voice.
In the 6th Rahu gives wealth and a long life, though the native is troubled by enemies and unseen forces and by diseases of the anus.
In the 7th Rahu brings loss of wealth through women, separation from the beloved, loss of vigour and self-willed folly.
In the 8th Rahu gives a short life, impure acts, a defect of a limb, wind disorders and few children.
In the 9th Rahu makes the native a headman of clan, village or city, but given to speaking against others and to unrighteous acts.
In the 10th Rahu gives fame and fearlessness and a hand in others' affairs, but few children and few good deeds.
In the 11th Rahu gives prosperity and a long life, but few children and trouble to the ears.
In the 12th Rahu brings secret sins, heavy spending and diseases from water.

Ke.text: In the Lagna Ketu makes the native ungrateful, unhappy and a tale-bearer, keeping bad company, with some deformity of the body.
In the 2nd Ketu leaves the native without learning or riches, coarse of speech and sinister of look, eating at others' tables.
In the 3rd Ketu gives a long life, strength, wealth and fame, happiness with the spouse and good food, but the loss of a brother.
In the 4th Ketu takes away lands, vehicles, mother and happiness; the native leaves the homeland and lives on others.
In the 5th Ketu brings loss of children, disease of the stomach and trouble from spirits, and an evil turn of mind.
In the 6th Ketu gives magnanimity, excellent qualities, lasting fame and authority, victory over enemies and wishes fulfilled.
In the 7th Ketu brings disrespect, bad company, disease of the bowels and loss of the spouse and of vitality.
In the 8th Ketu gives a short life, loss of dear friends, quarrels, wounds from weapons and failed undertakings.
In the 9th Ketu makes the native unrighteous and unlucky, poor and a slanderer of the good, and may take the father.
In the 10th Ketu brings obstacles to good deeds and impure acts, yet energy, boldness and renown.
In the 11th Ketu gives hoarded wealth, many good qualities, enjoyment of life and goals achieved.
In the 12th Ketu brings secret sins, wasteful spending on vile things, forbidden conduct and disease of the eyes.
